title: Establish resilient call choreography and backoff contract for idempotent and hedged flows
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Goal: define a single operational contract for retry, timeout and backoff behavior that spans client SDKs and the runtime, explicitly covering idempotency keys and hedged requests so multi-region failover and load-shedding behave predictably under SLO constraints.

Background: Multiple services and SDKs have drifted in backoff shape (linear vs exponential), default timeouts, and how idempotency keys are handled. During two recent incidents (regional GPU outage 2025-11 and chat spike 2026-01) inconsistent client retries caused cascading load and increased tail latency. We must codify behavior so clients, runtime, and control plane can coordinate: avoid amplification from aggressive retries, make hedging deterministic and observable, and ensure idempotency semantics are safe for downstream state.

Scope: clients (all official SDKs), external REST callers (via headers), and runtime routing (hosted/dedicated/private). Excludes legacy third-party clients (documented guidance only).

Proposal (high level):
- Retry/Backoff shape: jittered exponential backoff as canonical algorithm. Parameters: initial_backoff_ms=50, multiplier=2.0, max_backoff_ms=2000, max_attempts=3. Jitter mode: "full" (random between 0 and calculated backoff). Clients must expose this config and not exceed max_attempts unless explicitly opt-in and marked in metrics.
- Timeouts: per-request deadline must be explicit. Default client-side deadline = 10s for generation calls, 3s for metadata/health calls. SDKs will surface per-call deadline and enforce via cancellation. Runtime will respect client deadline header (X-Request-Deadline) for routing and not perform server-side retries beyond that deadline.
- Idempotency: header X-Idempotency-Key (uuidv4 recommended). Keys are required for any request that can mutate state (e.g., model fine-tune kickoffs, inference with billing events where duplicate billing is possible). Runtime stores idempotency entries with TTL = 24h for mutating operations, 1h for non-mutating dedupe (e.g., dedupe simple retries). The idempotency store must record status: IN_PROGRESS, SUCCEEDED, FAILED and provide safe response replays based on recorded response code and body hash. Clients must include a clear note in SDK docs about semantics and recommended reuse patterns.
- Hedging: hedged requests are allowed only for idempotent or read-only calls. Hedging policy: hedged_delay_ms = 40 (default), max_fanout = 2 (original + 1 hedge). Hedging must annotate traces with "hedge.slot" and emit metric "hedge.fanout". Runtime will cancel outstanding siblings on first write/read result. SDKs may opt out. Hedging must not be used for operations with side effects unless an idempotency key is present and the runtime de-duplicates via the idempotency store.
- Circuit breaker & load shedding: circuit break per-route with trip threshold based on error budget burn rate and p95 latency. Default trip config: failure_rate_threshold=0.20 over a 1m window OR p95_latency > SLA_multiplier*target (SLA_multiplier default 4). On trip: shed new requests at 10% progressive ramp, escalate to 100% over 30s if burn continues. Clients will receive HTTP 503 + Retry-After when event occurs. Runtime provides a per-customer and per-region breaker.
- Observability: mandate metrics and traces. Required metrics: retry.attempts (tags: route, client_language), retry.final_error, hedge.fanout, hedged.success_after_hedge, idempotency.reused, idempotency.store_latency_ms, circuit.trips, shed.rate. Tracing must include span attributes: "rh.idempotency_key", "rh.hedge_slot", "rh.retry_attempt", "rh.route_id".
- Compatibility & migration: introduce feature flag "rh.retry_contract_v2" on account level. Default for high-volume customers will be gradual rollout. SDKs will add opt-in config with clear opt-out.

Implementation tasks (short):
1) Runtime: idempotency store API and TTL enforcement, hedging orchestration hooks, circuit-breaker integration, metric names and tags (ENG runtime team).
2) SDKs: expose idempotency header helpers, default backoff implementation, per-call deadline handling, opt-in hedging toggle (SDK team).
3) Docs/Runbook: public API spec page, migration playbook, incident runbook updates for scenarios where client retries amplify load (DX/Docs).

API surface (headers):
- X-Idempotency-Key: <uuid> (optional except where mutating)
- X-Hedge-Request: "1" (clients request hedging by setting this header; runtime may ignore)
- X-Request-Deadline: epoch-ms deadline used for runtime scheduling
- X-Rh-Retry-Policy: "contract-v2" (explicit opt-in)

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime supports idempotency store with TTL and a deterministic replay policy (tests + perf benchmarks)
- SDKs across three languages (Python, Go, JS) implement the backoff crate and header helpers with test coverage
- Dashboards for retry amplification, hedged success, and idempotency reuse are live for top 20 routes
- Migration plan published and small cohort of customers moved behind feature flag with diagnostics enabled

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Increased complexity in runtime for idempotency storage and replay; storage cost vs safety tradeoff. Mitigation: per-account TTL limits and sampling.
- Hedging reduces median and tail latency but increases instantaneous load; kept conservative (max_fanout=2) and gated by route-level SLOs.
- Divergence with third-party clients: provide clear API-level headers and a compatibility doc, but cannot force behavior for external callers.

Security/Privacy: idempotency keys are treated as non-sensitive; do not log full payloads. If request bodies contain PII that would be stored on idempotency store, ensure minimal response hash is stored instead of full body.

Notes: see design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Retry+Contract+V2 and design diagram: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/xyz-retry-contract. Proposed RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/328
comments: 2026-02-22 - Liam O'Connor: Drafted initial spec after incident postmortem. Key open question: should hedging live in client or runtime? Recommendation: runtime orchestration + client opt-in so control plane can throttle hedges globally.

2026-02-25 - PM (Nora Chen): Agree with runtime-first hedging. Add requirement to expose per-account hinge to opt out. Request: include acceptance criteria for dashboards and alerting so SREs can detect amplification quickly.

2026-03-01 - Eng Review (Diego Ramos): Concern about idempotency store scale for high-cardinality ML requests. Suggest sampling for large customers and offline cache eviction. Action: add limit config per account and implement tombstone compaction. Assigned ENG-130412.

2026-03-04 - Security (Priya Malhotra): Confirmed idempotency keys are non-sensitive but flagged any stored request metadata must be scrubbed for PII. Added security checklist to runbook (see PR #452 in infra).

2026-03-08 - DX (Marta Silva): SDK API proposals uploaded: Python/JS/Go helpers and examples. Need PRs for each SDK which link to this ticket. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/799, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/614

2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented runtime idempotency prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2037. Benchmarked 95th percentile idempotency store read at 8ms under 10k qps. Next: integrate with circuit-breaker and hedging hooks.
